messages:
lia: Heads up — noticed a weird staging regression after the Go SDK warmup/prefetch change. Large batches get queued and CPU climbs until requests start 429ing.

sam: Can you paste the timeline/graphs? Is this only with embeddings or generation too? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

lia: Mostly embeddings batch job. Timeline: prefetch kicks in, we see a steady fanout of goroutines doing warmup calls, then upstream returns 429s, but the warmup keeps spawning more work for ~20s.

lia: Logs excerpt:
```
2026-03-22T10:12:05Z prefetch.go:118 spawn warmup worker id=7 page=0
2026-03-22T10:12:06Z http: response 429 model=embed-xxx retry-after=0.5
2026-03-22T10:12:07Z prefetch.go:118 spawn warmup worker id=8 page=1
2026-03-22T10:12:08Z http: response 429 model=embed-xxx retry-after=1.0
```

maya: That smells like a backpressure latch — warmup spawns up to N prefetch workers and they don't respect the global concurrency/semaphore when they retry. If retry logic doesn't signal upstream saturation (or disables warmup on repeated 429s) you'll amplify.

josh: FYI python SDK doesn't behave like this — our py prefetch halts warmup on repeated 429s. Looks like an SDK parity gap.

lia: Repro script attached in my gist but TL;DR config used: PageSize=128 Prefetch=6 Warmup=true. When I flip Prefetch=1 problem disappears.

sam: Quick mitigation for customers: set Prefetch=1 or disable Warmup. We'll add note to the onboarding doc.

maya: Long-term fix ideas:
- make prefetch workers acquire a global inflight token (semaphore) before actual call
- if a worker observes >=2 consecutive 429s, reduce its own prefetch factor or stop warmup for that paginator instance
- bubble throttling state into the shared client so other paginators can back off

josh: +1. Also we should check token refresh/race: if warmup triggers auth refresh concurrently with many inflight requests, you can get a transient auth-induced retries that bypass the client-level backoff.

retry-bot: detected 429 spike for client=go-sdk warmup-runner env=staging window=30s count=312

lia: I'll open an issue with traces, logs, and a minimal repro. Assigning to eng-devex, label: sdk-parity, severity: medium.

sam: Can you include a suggested quick patch? If small we can cherry-pick to a dot-release.

lia: Draft patch in branch: fix/go-prefetch-semaphore — basically add a buffered channel limiter and stop warmup after 2 consecutive 429s per-paginator.

maya: Nice. Also add a unit test that injects an artificial 429 error path and asserts warmup stops.

josh: I'll coordinate with docs to add a short note in Quickstart about prefetch defaults and how to tune for onboarding workloads.

lia: Thanks team. I'll drop the issue link and the traceback when I push the branch. :rocket:
